The "Compiled AI" paper (XY.AI Labs + Stanford/Cornell/Harvard): LLMs generate executable code artifacts during a COMPILATION phase; workflows then execute deterministically with ZERO further model invocation. Key elements: (i) constrained generation — narrow business-logic functions embedded in VALIDATED TEMPLATES; (ii) a FOUR-STAGE generation-and-validation pipeline converting probabilistic output into production-ready artifacts; (iii) an evaluation framework: token amortization (break-even ~17 transactions, 57x token reduction at 1,000 transactions), determinism, reliability, security (96.7% prompt-injection detection, 87.5% static code safety), cost. Results: 96% task completion on BFCL function-calling with zero execution tokens; Code Factory variant matches Direct LLM on DocILE key-field extraction (KILE 80.0%) with best line-item recognition (LIR 80.4%). Antecedents: DSPy declarative pipeline optimization, LLM+P hybrid neural-symbolic planning.
